Dependency edges between issues must be recorded with **GitHub's native issue-dependency
feature**, not a prose `## Depends on` / `## Blocks` section in the body.

**Why:** prose edges are error-prone. They are hand-maintained in two places, so the reverse
edge silently rots — an audit on 2026-08-02 found forward edges present and well-written on 17
recently-filed issues while **zero of seven** upstreams reciprocated. The native feature writes
both directions from a single call and surfaces in the issue UI and list filters, so it cannot
drift.

**How to apply** (the API is live on FSM1/cipher-box):

```bash
# add: issue N is blocked by issue M — pass M's DATABASE id, not its number
ID=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<M> --jq '.id')
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X POST \
  repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=$ID

`issue_id` is the numeric `.id`, NOT the issue number — passing the number silently targets the
wrong issue. Posting `blocked_by` on N makes N appear under M's `blocking` automatically; never

=== deploy-staging.yml
# Edited for v2 (blueprint/deploy.md). SendGrid stays, reached through the API's
# MAIL_PROVIDER seam. The gateway forward_auth wiring is the one v2 edit still
# outstanding.
name: Deploy Staging

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'staging-*'
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      staging_tag:
        required: true
        type: string
  # Before the first v2 release exists, WIP v2 deploys run from a dispatch
  # against a main SHA with no tag (blueprint/deploy.md).
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wipe_volumes:
        description: 'DESTRUCTIVE: drop the postgres and ipfs volumes before deploying (the cutover redeploy)'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  # A dispatch has no tag, so it ships the dispatched commit. Every value this
  # can take is also a valid checkout ref.
  DEPLOY_TAG: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.sha) || github.ref_name }}

permissions: {}

jobs:
  # A dispatch may select any ref, so the `main` SHA the trigger is scoped to
  # (blueprint/deploy.md) is asserted rather than assumed — this is also the
  # trigger that carries the destructive wipe.
  assert-main-revision:
    name: Assert the dispatched revision is on main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Assert the dispatched commit is an ancestor of main
        if: ${{ !inputs.staging_tag && github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DISPATCHED_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Base-to-head: an ancestor of main compares as `behind`, main's own
          # HEAD as `identical`; anything off main is `ahead` or `diverged`.
          status=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/compare/main...${DISPATCHED_SHA}" --jq '.status')
          case "${status}" in
            identical | behind)
              echo "${DISPATCHED_SHA} is on main (${status})"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Refusing to deploy ${DISPATCHED_SHA}: not a main revision (compare status: ${status}). Dispatch this workflow from main."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

  build-api:
    name: Build & Push API Image
    needs: [assert-main-revision]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-api" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Extract component versions
        id: versions
        run: |
          API_VERSION=$(node -e "console.log(require('./apps/api/package.json').version)")
          echo "api=${API_VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: apps/api/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ steps.versions.outputs.api }}
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:latest-staging
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

  build-caddy:
    name: Build & Push Caddy Image
    needs: [assert-main-revision]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "CADDY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-caddy" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631027851001ddb9b187196cc803df7f5f0e # v4.3.0

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: docker/caddy
          push: true
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=caddy-front
          tags: |
            ${{ env.CADDY_IMAGE }}:latest-staging
            ${{ env.CADDY_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

  build-web:
    name: Build Web App
    needs: [assert-main-revision]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

      # apps/web compiles crates/wasm into the engine artifact it bundles.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/wasm-bindgen-cli

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Kept separate from the bundle step so the staging secrets below never
      # enter the environment of a cargo build script.
      - name: Build the engine WASM artifact
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:wasm

      - name: Build web app with staging env vars
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:bundle
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.API_URL }}
          # Unset leaves the content gateway dormant: reads fail closed as
          # unavailable rather than reaching for an unconfigured endpoint.
          VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: ${{ vars.VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL }}
          # Unset falls back to the public endpoint, so the self-hosted resolve
          # leg behind the member front is only reached once this names it.
          VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS: ${{ vars.VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS }}
          VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS: ${{ vars.VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_FARO_URL: ${{ vars.VITE_FARO_URL }}
          GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_STACK_ID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_STACK_ID }}

      - name: Upload web dist as artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: apps/web/dist/
          retention-days: 1

  deploy-vps:
    name: Deploy to Staging VPS
    needs: [build-api, build-caddy, build-web]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

      - name: Download web dist artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: web-dist/

      # appleboy's actions skip host-key verification entirely when `fingerprint`
      # is empty, so a missing or malformed value must fail the job here rather
      # than open an unverified connection.
      - name: Require a pinned host key
        env:
          SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
        run: |
          case "$SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT" in
            SHA256:?*) ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::the staging environment needs SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT set to the host key's SHA256 fingerprint: ssh-keyscan HOST | ssh-keygen -lf - | cut -d' ' -f2"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

      # The API refuses to boot in a deployed profile without these, and this job
      # has no post-deploy health gate, so an unset value lands as a green deploy
      # over a crash-looping container.
      - name: Require the identity and mail configuration
        env:
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          MAIL_PROVIDER: ${{ vars.MAIL_PROVIDER }}
          SENDGRID_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SENDGRID_API_KEY }}
          MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: ${{ vars.MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS }}
        run: |
          for name in GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY MAIL_PROVIDER SENDGRID_API_KEY MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "::error::the staging environment needs $name set"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          if [ "$MAIL_PROVIDER" != "sendgrid" ]; then
            echo "::error::staging needs MAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid; 'log' delivers no mail and the API refuses it outside development"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Generate .env.staging
        run: |
          cat > .env.staging << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=staging
          CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=${{ secrets.TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          PORT=3000
          DB_HOST=postgres
          DB_PORT=5432
          DB_USERNAME=${{ vars.DB_USERNAME }}
          DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}
          DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_staging
          JWT_SECRET=${{ secrets.JWT_SECRET }}
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${{ vars.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS }}
          # Two entries arrive from the Caddyfile's trusted_proxies; the Lint
          # gate holds the pair together (blueprint/deploy.md).
          TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=2
          KUBO_API_URL=http://ipfs:5001
          ROUTING_V1_URL=http://someguy:8190
          THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=${{ secrets.THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_URL }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          MAIL_PROVIDER=${{ vars.MAIL_PROVIDER }}
          SENDGRID_API_KEY=${{ secrets.SENDGRID_API_KEY }}
          MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=${{ vars.MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS }}
          ENVEOF
          # Append image tag, lowercase owner, and component versions (can't use shell vars in quoted heredoc)
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          echo "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=${OWNER,,}" >> .env.staging
          echo "TAG=${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}" >> .env.staging
          API_VER=$(node -e "console.log(require('./apps/api/package.json').version)")
          echo "API_VERSION=${API_VER}" >> .env.staging

      - name: Copy files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          source: '.env.staging,docker/docker-compose.staging.yml,docker/Caddyfile,docker/csp.caddy,docker/alloy-config.river,docker/ipfs-init/001-provide-strategy.sh'
          target: /opt/cipherbox
          strip_components: 0

      - name: Arrange files on VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          script: |
            # Move files to correct locations
            mv /opt/cipherbox/.env.staging /opt/cipherbox/docker/.env.staging 2>/dev/null || true
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Docker Compose reads .env automatically for variable substitution
            cp .env.staging .env

            # Restrict env file permissions (contains secrets)
            chmod 600 .env .env.staging

            # Ensure certs symlink exists for Caddy
            rm -rf /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs
            ln -sf /opt/cipherbox/certs /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs

      - name: Deploy web app files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          source: 'web-dist/*'
          target: /opt/cipherbox/web
          strip_components: 1
          rm: true

      # The cutover redeploy (blueprint/deploy.md). `wipe_volumes` is declared
      # under `workflow_dispatch` alone, so no other trigger can set it — a
      # `workflow_call` caller may only pass the inputs that trigger declares,
      # and `github.event_name` is the *caller's* event on that path, which
      # makes it useless as a second gate here. Caddy's volumes are left alone:
      # they hold the issued TLS certificates.
      - name: Wipe the staging data volumes
        if: inputs.wipe_volumes
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml down
            # `down --volumes` would take Caddy's with it, so select the two
            # declared names out of this project by compose's own labels.
            for declared in postgres_staging ipfs_staging; do
              vols=$(docker volume ls -q \
                --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=cipherbox-staging" \
                --filter "label=com.docker.compose.volume=${declared}")
              if [ -n "${vols}" ]; then
                echo "${vols}" | xargs docker volume rm
              else
                echo "no ${declared} volume to remove"
              fi
            done

      - name: Deploy services
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Login to GHCR
            echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin

            # Set image tag from git tag (GHCR requires lowercase owner)
            export TAG="${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}"
            OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
            export GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER="${OWNER,,}"

            # Pull new images
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml pull

            # Run database migrations before starting services
            # (api service inherits env vars from env_file in compose)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
              api node dist/run-migrations.js

            # Start/restart services
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d

            # Restart Caddy to pick up refreshed web files bind mount
            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml restart caddy

            # Cleanup old images
            docker image prune -f

  provision-dashboard:
    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
    needs: [deploy-vps]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

      - name: Wait for Grafana Cloud readiness
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required for Grafana readiness check}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required for Grafana readiness check}"
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
          MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
          INTERVAL=10
          for ((i=1; i<=MAX_ATTEMPTS; i++)); do
            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 \
              -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
              "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/health") || HTTP_CODE=000
            if [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "200" ]]; then
              echo "Grafana Cloud is ready (attempt $i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
              exit 0
            elif [[ "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^(401|403|404)$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Grafana returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE — check GRAFANA_URL and GRAFANA_API_KEY"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Grafana not ready (HTTP $HTTP_CODE), waiting ${INTERVAL}s... ($i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
            sleep "$INTERVAL"
          done
          echo "::error::Grafana Cloud did not become ready after $((MAX_ATTEMPTS * INTERVAL))s"
          exit 1

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"

          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
                 'del(.__inputs)
                  | .id = null
                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

          if [[ ! "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Grafana API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json

# Releases & Versioning

Normative source: `blueprint/deploy.md` in [FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next). One product version, one release train.

- The repo releases as a single product `vX.Y.Z` (starting at `v2.0.0`). One release-please component (root, `include-component-in-tag: false`), one CHANGELOG. There is no per-package versioning: internal packages and crates are version-frozen and never published; releases never touch `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.
- Version surfaces are exactly two files: root `package.json` (manifest source) and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (via `extra-files`). Both agree with `.release-please-manifest.json`; a release moves all three together.
- `release-please.yml` runs on every push to `main` and keeps one open release PR. Merging that PR mints the `vX.Y.Z` tag and the GitHub Release that `desktop-release.yml` attaches installers to and `tag-staging.yml` asserts on.
- `release-please-config.json` pins `release-as: "2.0.0"` to mint the first v2 release from a `1.0.0` manifest. **Delete that pin in the first PR after the `chore: release v2.0.0` PR merges** — while it stands, every later release re-mints 2.0.0.
- The release path writes nothing to PR branches. The v1 preview-bot (`pr-release-preview.yml`), `release-gate.yml`, and `cargo-lock-release-sync.yml` are deleted — do not resurrect the pattern of bot commits on PR branches.
- Staging deploys are triggered by `staging-*` tags via `tag-staging.yml` (manual dispatch → release-tag assertion → e2e gates → `staging-approval` → tag → `deploy-staging.yml`). Pre-v2.0.0 staging deploys of WIP v2 go via `workflow_dispatch` of `deploy-staging.yml` at a `main` SHA.
- v1 is frozen: branch `v1` / tag `v1-freeze` at `07376d0b` (cipher-box-v0.45.1). No new v1 releases. Only the final v1 product release `cipher-box-v0.45.2` is retained (until the first v2.0.0 release is cut); all other v1 tags, per-package release tags, and `staging-*` tags have been pruned — v1 will not be redeployed to staging before the v2 cutover.

# CipherBox Staging - Caddy Reverse Proxy & Web App
# Cloudflare Origin CA certificates for Full (Strict) SSL mode
# Cloudflare handles browser-facing TLS; Caddy handles CF-to-origin TLS
{
	auto_https off

	order rate_limit before basicauth

	# Trusting Cloudflare's ranges is what makes an IP-keyed limit key on a member
	# rather than on a whole edge POP (blueprint/deploy.md). Mirrors
	# cloudflare.com/ips; the Lint gate pins the set.
	#
	# `{client_ip}` reads CF-Connecting-IP, which Cloudflare writes itself and
	# overwrites on the way in, rather than X-Forwarded-For, which it APPENDS to —
	# leaving every entry left of the caller's own under the caller's control.
	# Strict then refuses to believe either header from an untrusted peer.
	# Verified: a caller whose own address is inside a Cloudflare range made
	# X-Forwarded-For resolve to an entry it wrote, and one bucket per forged
	# address is no bucket at all.
	servers {
		trusted_proxies_strict
		client_ip_headers CF-Connecting-IP
		trusted_proxies static 173.245.48.0/20 103.21.244.0/22 103.22.200.0/22 103.31.4.0/22 141.101.64.0/18 108.162.192.0/18 190.93.240.0/20 188.114.96.0/20 197.234.240.0/22 198.41.128.0/17 162.158.0.0/15 104.16.0.0/13 104.24.0.0/14 172.64.0.0/13 131.0.72.0/22 2400:cb00::/32 2606:4700::/32 2803:f800::/32 2405:b500::/32 2405:8100::/32 2a06:98c0::/29 2c0f:f248::/32
	}

	# Caddy's error log records client IP beside the requested URI, which re-links
	# an account to its reads — the accelerator front must stay silent there too.
	# The rate limiter logs each refusal under its own namespace, outside any
	# vhost's access log, so it needs naming here rather than inheriting silence.
	log accelerator_errors {
		output discard
		include http.log.error.accelerator http.handlers.rate_limit
	}
}

# Cloudflare names the caller in headers of its own beside X-Forwarded-For, and
# CF-Ray is the id its logs record next to the requested path — the join key
# between a pseudonym at the verify leg and a CID at the accelerator. Nothing
# that identifies a reader may reach an upstream whose stdout ships offsite
# (blueprint/api.md, Egress).
(strip_caller) {
	header_up -CF-Connecting-IP
	header_up -CF-Connecting-IPv6
	header_up -CF-Pseudo-IPv4
	header_up -CF-EW-Via
	header_up -CF-Worker
	header_up -CF-IPCountry
	header_up -CF-Visitor
	header_up -CF-Ray
	header_up -CDN-Loop
	header_up -True-Client-IP
	header_up -X-Real-IP
	header_up -Forwarded
}

# The ranges above are Cloudflare's, not this zone's: any tenant can point a
# proxied record at the origin address and arrive from inside a trusted range.
# The zone's own origin-pull certificate is what closes that; the shared
# Cloudflare origin-pull CA is the same hole, since every tenant presents it.
# Caddy routes on Host and not on SNI, so a vhost left unauthenticated admits
# them all under a forged one — the gate is uniform (blueprint/deploy.md).
(origin_tls) {
	tls /etc/caddy/certs/origin.pem /etc/caddy/certs/origin-key.pem {
		client_auth {
			# `verify_if_given` would admit a caller that simply presents none.
			mode require_and_verify
			trust_pool file {
				pem_file /etc/caddy/certs/cloudflare-zone-origin-pull-ca.pem
			}
		}
	}
}

api-staging.cipherbox.cc {
	import origin_tls
	respond /metrics 403
	reverse_proxy api:3000
}

app-staging.cipherbox.cc {
	import origin_tls
	root * /srv/web

	import /etc/caddy/csp.caddy

	# Fingerprinted assets must 404 when absent; the SPA fallback would otherwise
	# answer a missing script or wasm module with a 200 text/html index.html.
	handle /assets/* {
		file_server
	}

	handle {
		try_files {path} /index.html
		file_server
	}
}

# Read-accelerator front. Args: {args[0]} upstream, {args[1]} CORS methods.
# Obligations per blueprint/api.md (Egress).
(accelerator_front) {
	import origin_tls

	# The raw pseudonym in an access log is a gateway credential at rest, and a
	# client IP recorded beside a read re-links the account.
	log accelerator {
		output discard
	}

	header {
		Access-Control-Allow-Origin "{$ACCELERATOR_ALLOWED_ORIGIN:https://app-staging.cipherbox.cc}"
		Access-Control-Expose-Headers "Content-Length, Content-Range, Content-Type"
		# `+` appends; setting it would drop the upstream's own Vary members.
		+Vary Origin
	}

	# A preflight carries no Authorization, so gating it would 401 every browser read.
	@preflight method OPTIONS
	handle @preflight {
		header {
			Access-Control-Allow-Methods "{args[1]}"
			Access-Control-Allow-Headers "Authorization, Range, Accept"
			Access-Control-Max-Age "86400"
		}
		respond 204
	}

	# Reads present the pseudonym, writes never do (blueprint/api.md, Egress), so
	# the gate takes only the read methods: a read token cannot become a write
	# upstream, whatever the accelerator would have accepted.
	@read method GET HEAD
	handle @read {
		# The verify leg never learns the path, so never account+CID per read; the
		# deletes drop client-supplied copies too. X-Forwarded-For stays — the API
		# rate-limits this surface per client. Range and Accept would describe the
		# read as surely as the path: the byte window and block-vs-CAR shape.
		reverse_proxy api:3000 {
			method GET
			rewrite /auth/gateway/verify?
			header_up -X-Forwarded-Host
			header_up -X-Forwarded-Uri
			header_up -X-Forwarded-Method
			header_up -Range
			header_up -Accept
			header_up -Referer
			header_up -CF-Ray

			# An empty handle_response continues to the content proxy below.
			@alive status 204
			handle_response @alive {
			}

			# Deny on any non-204, so a verify-side fault fails closed.
			handle_response {
				respond 403
			}
		}

		# An accelerator's stdout ships offsite, and an IP logged beside a CID
		# re-links the account as surely as the pseudonym would.
		reverse_proxy {args[0]} {
			header_up -Authorization
			header_up -X-Forwarded-For
			import strip_caller
		}
	}

	handle {
		header Allow "{args[1]}"
		respond 405
	}
}

gateway-staging.cipherbox.cc {
	import accelerator_front ipfs:8080 "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS"
}

routing-staging.cipherbox.cc {
	# Signed IPNS records are self-authenticating, so publishing needs no token.
	# The snippet's gate takes only GET and HEAD and its refusal is an unmatched
	# `handle`, which Caddy orders last, so this wins the PUT wherever the import
	# sits.
	@publish {
		method PUT
		path /routing/v1/ipns/*
	}
	handle @publish {
		# An IPNS record is a couple of KB. This cap and the rate below are the
		# whole abuse budget of the leg.
		request_body {
			max_size 64KB
		}

		# Jitter blunts Retry-After: exact, it tells whoever shares an egress address
		# with a member when that member last published, which is scope-mutation
		# timing. A /128 is no bucket at all — a caller holding the usual delegated
		# IPv6 /64 rotates the interface ID per request — so the limiter masks the
		# key to that /64 before it buckets.
		rate_limit {
			jitter 0.5
			zone publish {
				key {client_ip}
				ipv6_prefix 64
				events 60
				window 1m
			}
		}
		reverse_proxy someguy:8190 {
			header_up -Authorization
			header_up -X-Forwarded-For
			import strip_caller
		}
	}

	import accelerator_front someguy:8190 "GET, HEAD, PUT, OPTIONS"
}

# Without a catch-all site Caddy appends a matcher-less connection policy of its
# own, and that one carries no `client_auth` — an unmatched SNI would then reach
# Host-based routing with no certificate presented.
https:// {
	import origin_tls
	abort
}

:80 {
	redir https://{host}{uri} permanent
}

/**
 * Programmatic migration runner for Docker containers.
 *
 * The TypeORM CLI (via ts-node) is not available in production images.
 * This script runs migrations using compiled JS entities and migrations.
 *
 * Usage (inside Docker container):
 *   node dist/run-migrations.js
 */
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { config } from 'dotenv';

config();

const dataSource = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres',
  host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
  port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432', 10),
  username: process.env.DB_USERNAME || 'postgres',
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || 'postgres',
  database: process.env.DB_DATABASE || 'cipherbox',
  entities: ['dist/**/*.entity.js'],
  migrations: ['dist/migrations/*.js'],
  logging: ['error', 'migration'],
});

async function run() {
  try {
    await dataSource.initialize();
    console.log('Running migrations...');
    const migrations = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (migrations.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');
    } else {
      console.log(`Applied ${migrations.length} migration(s):`);
      for (const m of migrations) {
        console.log(`  - ${m.name}`);
      }
    }
    await dataSource.destroy();
    console.log('Migrations complete.');
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    console.error(
      'Migration failed:',
      err.name || 'UnknownError',
      err.message?.replace(/((?:host|password|user(?:name)?)=)[^\s;,]+/gi, '$1***') || ''
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
